answer_1.quote: We propose CSJ as a downstream task of text simplification and cross-lingual scientific summarization to generate a coherent cross-lingual popular science story. ... We empirically evaluate the performance of SSR against several existing CLS models on the WIKIPEDIA dataset ... and on the SPEKTRUM dataset.
answer_1.outputs: German popular‑science summaries generated from English scientific articles

answer_2.quote: We evaluate all models with three metrics: (1) ROUGE (Lin, 2004) -R1 and R2 compute the uni‑ and bi‑gram overlaps ... (2) BERT‑score (BS) captures far‑away dependencies ... (3) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease (FRE) computes text readability ...

answer_4.quote: We hired five annotators and provide them with 25 randomly selected outputs (of each model) from SSR and mBART with their original texts and gold references. ... The annotators were asked to evaluate each document for three linguistic properties on a Likert scale from 1 to 5. ... We asked annotators to evaluate each summary for the following features: Relevance, Fluency, Simplicity, Overall Ranking.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators evaluated each generated summary on a Likert scale (1‑5) for relevance, fluency, simplicity and overall ranking compared to the gold reference.
